help.stdout:
usage: gnd conformance [-h] [--format {text,json}] model directory

Ask whether a project `gnd codegen` generated still agrees with the model it
came from. FOUR assertions run. Two are exact and corroborating: INTEGRITY —
every code-emitted file still hashes to what the codegen manifest recorded —
and CURRENCY, the manifest's model digest against the model's digest now,
which IS model-code drift: the model moved and the code did not. Both are
importable functions rather than CLI-only paths, so a downstream tool can
invoke them without going through argv. The third is STRUCTURAL, and it is the
assertion that makes a green result mean anything: the emitted surface is
checked against the fact types the MODEL declares, computed from the model and
the filesystem and never from the manifest or a previous generation. Without
it the other two establish only that the generator agrees with itself — a
project that is well-formed and empty, with every digest re-signed, passes
both. The fourth is ARCHITECTURE: authored module, symbol, artifact and entry-
point declarations are compared with static filesystem and AST observations
without executing the project. Fully offline over committed artifacts, and the
generated project is NEVER imported — this command reads bytes and hashes
them, because importing a module to inspect it would execute the project's own
code on every CI run. What a GREEN result does not say travels in the payload,
not only in this text: every file the manifest records appears in either
`examined` or `unexamined` by integrity, and extension files (pyproject.toml,
references/) are not digest-gated because human- and LLM-authored text is not
byte-reproducible and cannot be digest-gated, and the required `limits` block
names the manifest co-edit blind spot — a manifest cannot record its own
digest, so a derived file edited TOGETHER with its manifest entry is
undetectable by digest comparison, exactly as in `gnd doctor`. Two runs over
one unchanged project print byte-identical JSON. Exits 0 when all four
assertions ran and found nothing, 13 when the generated code no longer matches
its model (one band for the whole command — the payload names which assertion
and which file), 3 when the codegen manifest will not parse, 64 on usage
errors, 66 when the manifest or the model is missing so nothing could be
compared at all (fail closed — a check that could not run must not read as one
that passed), 74 when the project tree could not be read.

positional arguments:
  model                 path to the model file
  directory             the generated project's root (the directory `gnd
                        codegen --out` wrote)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --format {text,json}  output rendering: human-readable text (default) or one
                        JSON payload
